synopsis: The Machinery Regulation applies from 20 January 2027, before the braking prototype arrives, and EU acceptance of collision-mitigation systems runs through machinery conformity rather than a separate route [f361, f6696, f7754, f2009]. Annex I Part A covers self-evolving machine-learning safety components and machinery embedding them, with notified-body involvement required; whether a trained-then-frozen detector qualifies remains disputed, and notified-body lead time alone could exceed the four-month validation window [f2090, f363, f2091, f11928]. The corpus reports that Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 was adopted on 8 July 2026 and entered into force on 27 July 2026, shifting machinery high-risk AI obligations to 2 August 2028 and leaving machinery-specific AI requirements to a delegated act [f2093, f2094, f6699]. The Product Liability Directive applies to products placed on the market after 9 December 2026, treats software as a product, and allows court-ordered disclosure for those products [f51, f9462, f10451]. Acceptance of simulation evidence remains uncertain, with neither guidance nor the outside assessor identified; some chapters relied on secondary legal summaries or did not verify the regulation, so users after October 2026 are advised to re-check regulatory dates [f8184, f8185, f8242, f9463, f4335, f55]. The supplied facts provide no substantive Data Act requirements, leaving that part of the four-law hub uncovered.
